title: 1 Kings 1
paragraphs: ¹ King David was old and advanced in years. His servants wrapped him in blankets, but he could not get warm. ² So his servants said to him, "Let us find a young virgin for my lord the king. She can attend him and care for him, and sleep beside him so that my lord the king may stay warm." ³ They searched throughout all Israel for a beautiful young woman and found Abishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king. ⁴ The young woman was very beautiful. She cared for the king and attended to his needs, but the king did not sleep with her. ⁵ Meanwhile Adonijah, the son of Haggith, began promoting himself, saying, "I will be king." He acquired chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run ahead of him.

⁶ His father had never once corrected him, never said, "Why do you behave this way?" Adonijah was also very handsome, and his mother had given birth to him after Absalom. ⁷ He conspired with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they supported his claim. ⁸ But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's elite warriors did not side with Adonijah. ⁹ Adonijah held a great sacrifice of sheep, oxen, and fattened cattle at the Stone of Zoheleth, near En Rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah who served the king. ¹⁰ But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the king's elite warriors, or his brother Solomon.

¹¹ Nathan went to Bathsheba, the mother of Solomon, and asked, "Have you not heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith has made himself king, and our lord David doesn't even know it? ¹² Let me give you advice so that you can save your own life and the life of your son Solomon. ¹³ Go in to King David and say to him, 'Didn't you, my lord the king, swear to me your servant that my son Solomon would reign after you and sit on your throne? Why then is Adonijah king?' ¹⁴ While you are still speaking with the king, I will come in after you and confirm what you have said." ¹⁵ Bathsheba went to the king in his room. The king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was caring for him.

¹⁶ Bathsheba bowed down and knelt before the king. "What do you want?" the king asked. ¹⁷ She said to him, "My lord, you swore to me your servant by the LORD your God: 'Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.' ¹⁸ But now, without your knowledge, Adonijah has become king. ¹⁹ He has sacrificed oxen, fattened cattle, and sheep in great numbers. He has invited all the king's sons, Abiathar the priest, and Joab the commander of the army — but he has not invited Solomon your servant. ²⁰ And now, my lord the king, all Israel is looking to you to tell them who will sit on the throne after you.

²¹ Otherwise, when you, my lord the king, die and lie with your ancestors, my son Solomon and I will be treated as criminals." ²² While she was still speaking with the king, the prophet Nathan arrived. ²³ They told the king, "Nathan the prophet is here." He came in before the king and bowed with his face to the ground. ²⁴ "My lord the king," Nathan said, "have you declared that Adonijah shall reign after you and sit on your throne? ²⁵ For he has gone down today and sacrificed vast numbers of oxen, fattened cattle, and sheep. He has invited all the king's sons, the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest — and right now they are eating and drinking with him and shouting, 'Long live King Adonijah!'

²⁶ But me, your servant — he has not invited me, nor Zadok the priest, nor Benaiah son of Jehoiada, nor your servant Solomon. ²⁷ Has this been done by my lord the king without telling your servants who should sit on the throne after you?" ²⁸ King David then said, "Call Bathsheba to me." She came before the king and stood in his presence. ²⁹ The king swore an oath: "As the LORD lives — who has delivered me from every trouble — ³⁰ I will do this very day what I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel: Solomon your son shall be king after me, and he shall sit on my throne in my place."

³¹ Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and knelt before the king. "May my lord King David live forever!" she said. ³² King David then said, "Summon Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada." They came before the king, ³³ and the king said to them, "Take your lord's servants with you, put my son Solomon on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon. ³⁴ There let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him king over Israel. Sound the trumpet and shout, 'Long live King Solomon!' ³⁵ Then come back up with him, and he will sit on my throne and reign in my place. I have appointed him ruler over Israel and Judah."

³⁶ Benaiah son of Jehoiada replied to the king, "Amen! May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, declare it so. ³⁷ As the LORD has been with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon, and may he make Solomon's throne even greater than the throne of my lord King David." ³⁸ Then Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and Pelethites set out. They put Solomon on King David's own mule and brought him to Gihon. ³⁹ Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon. Then they sounded the trumpet, and all the people shouted, "Long live King Solomon!" ⁴⁰ All the people came up behind him, playing flutes and celebrating with great joy. The noise was so great that the ground shook with the sound.

⁴¹ Adonijah and all his guests heard it just as they were finishing their meal. When Joab heard the sound of the trumpet, he said, "What is all that noise in the city?" ⁴² Even as he was speaking, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest arrived. "Come in," said Adonijah, "for you are a man of good standing and you bring good news." ⁴³ But Jonathan replied, "No — our lord King David has made Solomon king. ⁴⁴ The king sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites. They put him on the king's mule, ⁴⁵ and Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him king at Gihon. They have come back up rejoicing, and the whole city is in an uproar. That is the noise you heard.

⁴⁶ Solomon has now taken his seat on the royal throne. ⁴⁷ Moreover, the king's servants have come to bless our lord King David, saying, 'May God make Solomon's name even greater than yours, and may his throne be greater than your throne.' And the king bowed in worship on his bed. ⁴⁸ The king also said, 'Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who has today given someone to sit on my throne while I can still see it with my own eyes.'" ⁴⁹ At that, all Adonijah's guests got up in terror and scattered. ⁵⁰ Adonijah himself was terrified of Solomon. He went and took hold of the horns of the altar.

⁵¹ Word reached Solomon: "Adonijah is afraid of you. He has taken hold of the horns of the altar and says, 'Let King Solomon swear to me today that he will not kill his servant with the sword.'" ⁵² Solomon replied, "If he proves himself a man of character, not one hair of his head will fall to the ground. But if evil is found in him, he will die." ⁵³ So King Solomon sent for Adonijah, and they brought him down from the altar. He came and bowed down before King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, "Go home."
